```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, error = FALSE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE)
```

## Notebook Overview

**Inputs:**

- `../../../data-raw-temp/census/tab20_tract20_tract10_st06.txt` — the U.S.
  Census Bureau's UTF-8, pipe-delimited 2020-to-2010 California tract relationship
  file. Each row describes a geographic intersection; the raw file is read-only.

**Outputs:**

- `../../../data/xwalk_tr20_tr10.feather` — one row per California 2020 tract,
  with consistency/classification diagnostics and a 2010 key wherever uniquely
  defined. See [the output schema](schemas/xwalk_tr20_tr10.md).
- Pair-level `tract_relationships`, statewide/target-county QA summaries, and
  rejected one-to-one pair diagnostics remain in notebook memory.

**Steps:**

1. Set up environment
2. Read and validate source intersections
3. Characterize tract relationships
4. Construct the tract-level crosswalk
5. Review geographic diagnostics
6. Save and validate the output

For later ACS comparison, select `geo_consistent == 1`, join native-2020 2024
tract measures on `tr2020_id`, then 2016 measures on the explicit `tr2010_id`.
This notebook does not join ACS data, allocate changed tracts, or impose the
Step 2 county sample. `04_assemble_tract_panel.Rmd` uses this crosswalk for notebook-only
geographic coverage and consistent-pair measurement diagnostics; canonical
source selection and saved panel fields remain unchanged. The historical
`tract_change.feather` has a different contract and is preserved.

# 1. Set up environment

## 1.1 Load packages and helpers

Use the pipeline's existing packages. Source validation, relationship
characterization, tract reduction, and output checks live in
`R/tract_change_helpers.R`; shared reporting and key/schema assertions use the
existing helpers.

```{r load-packages-and-helpers}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(arrow)
library(knitr)

source(here::here("R", "helpers.R"))
source(here::here("R", "geography_qa.R"))
source(here::here("R", "tract_change_helpers.R"))
```

## 1.2 Configure paths and saving

Notebook reruns replace the existing crosswalk, as authorized by the analyst.
Each replacement is announced and validated before saving and after reloading.
Set `overwrite_output <- FALSE` to opt back into refusing an existing destination.

```{r set-paths}
source_path <- here::here("..", "..", "..", "data-raw-temp", "census",
                          "tab20_tract20_tract10_st06.txt")
output_path <- here::here("..", "..", "..", "data", "xwalk_tr20_tr10.feather")
overwrite_output <- TRUE
```

## 1.3 Configure target-county diagnostics

The county definitions match `step2_target_counties()` in `R/geography_qa.R`, used by both Step 2 notebooks; a focused test checks that
they stay synchronized. They apply only to diagnostic summaries of the completed
statewide crosswalk. Counties are assigned using the 2020 tract GEOID, and
partner counts retain the complete California relationship-file universe.

```{r target-county-config}
southern_california_counties <- c(
  "Los Angeles" = "037", "Orange" = "059", "Riverside" = "065",
  "San Bernardino" = "071", "Ventura" = "111"
)
bay_area_counties <- c(
  "Alameda" = "001", "Contra Costa" = "013", "Marin" = "041", "Napa" = "055",
  "San Francisco" = "075", "San Mateo" = "081", "Santa Clara" = "085",
  "Solano" = "095", "Sonoma" = "097"
)
target_county_lookup <- bind_rows(
  tibble(region = "Bay Area", county = names(bay_area_counties),
         county_fips = unname(bay_area_counties)),
  tibble(region = "Southern California", county = names(southern_california_counties),
         county_fips = unname(southern_california_counties))
)
assert_unique_key(target_county_lookup, "county_fips", "Target county lookup")
```

# 2. Read and validate source intersections

## 2.1 Import land areas and geographic keys

### Decision: Preserve the complete source relationship universe

Read only the two GEOIDs and three land-area fields. Preserve all intersections,
including rows with zero intersection land and 2010 partners outside California.
No county, state-of-2010, or positive-land filter precedes partner counting.
Both GEOIDs must be 11-digit character strings; only the 2020 ID must start
with `06`. Non-California 2010 IDs are valid source partners, not malformed IDs.

Land areas are whole square meters and can exceed 32-bit integer capacity.
Use doubles and require nonnegative, finite, integer-valued inputs below `2^53`
so exact area comparisons are preserved. Missing/malformed fields, duplicate
pairs, inconsistent repeated tract totals, and intersections exceeding a tract
total stop execution rather than being repaired or discarded. Other source
fields, including water areas, are not imported or used in diagnostics.

```{r read-relationships}
stopifnot("Missing Census relationship file" = file.exists(source_path))
source_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(source_path))
source_provenance <- tibble(
  source_file = source_path,
  source_bytes = file.info(source_path)$size,
  source_md5 = source_md5
)
print(source_provenance, width = Inf)

source_relationships <- read_delim(
  source_path, delim = "|", locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"),
  col_types = cols_only(
    GEOID_TRACT_20 = col_character(), AREALAND_TRACT_20 = col_double(),
    GEOID_TRACT_10 = col_character(), AREALAND_TRACT_10 = col_double(),
    AREALAND_PART = col_double()
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE
)
stopifnot("Relationship-file parse problems" = nrow(problems(source_relationships)) == 0L)
source_relationships <- source_relationships |>
  transmute(
    tr2020_id = GEOID_TRACT_20, tr2010_id = GEOID_TRACT_10,
    arealand_2020 = AREALAND_TRACT_20, arealand_2010 = AREALAND_TRACT_10,
    arealand_part = AREALAND_PART
  )
report_n(source_relationships, "Complete source intersections imported (no filtering)")
assert_tract_relationship_source(source_relationships)
```

# 3. Characterize tract relationships

## 3.1 Count partners and apply the analyst's land-consistency rule

### Decision: Require one-to-one, positive-land, exact overlap in both directions

A pair is geographically consistent only when all six conditions hold:

1. `n_2010_partners == 1`;
2. `n_2020_partners == 1`;
3. `arealand_2020 > 0`;
4. `arealand_2010 > 0`;
5. `arealand_part == arealand_2020`; and
6. `arealand_part == arealand_2010`.

Partner counts are distinct-ID counts from the complete source. There is no
near-match threshold. `same_geoid` is diagnostic only: equal IDs cannot rescue
changed land boundaries, and different IDs do not disqualify a consistent pair.
Flags use numeric double 0/1 values, matching existing data-quality flags.

Calculate each share as intersection land divided by that vintage's tract land.
A zero denominator produces `NA`; a positive denominator remains eligible for
its share calculation even when the other tract has zero land. Either zero
tract total sets `zero_land_area = 1` and precludes consistency. A zero-valued
intersection between two positive-land tracts is still a counted relationship.

```{r characterize-relationships}
tract_relationships <- characterize_tract_relationships(source_relationships)
report_n(tract_relationships, "Characterized pairs (all source rows preserved)",
         nrow(source_relationships))
stopifnot("Characterization changed source rows or values" = identical(
  select(tract_relationships, all_of(names(source_relationships))), source_relationships
))
```

# 4. Construct the tract-level crosswalk

## 4.1 Retain unique links and classify each 2020 tract

### Decision: Preserve unique keys without selecting a dominant partner

Every source 2020 tract receives one output row and retains its 2020 land total.
When exactly one 2010 partner exists, retain that partner's ID, reverse count,
`same_geoid`, land totals/intersection, and defined shares, including on changed
tracts. Otherwise all pair-specific fields are `NA`. No dominant partner is
selected. The unique-link join must preserve the complete 2020 key set without
row multiplication. Full pair diagnostics remain in `tract_relationships`.

### Decision: Any reverse multiplicity makes a multi-partner tract many-to-many

The analyst selected this rule for mixed pair-level classes. A 2020 tract with
multiple 2010 partners is `many_to_many` if **any** partner has multiple 2020
partners; otherwise it is `merge`. Retain `max_n_2020_partners` to audit this
distinction. With a single 2010 partner, reverse multiplicity is `split`;
otherwise use `consistent` or `one_to_one_changed` according to the six-condition
rule. At tract level, `zero_land_area` marks **any** zero-land-area relationship.

```{r build-crosswalk}
tract_crosswalk <- build_tract_crosswalk(tract_relationships)
assert_tract_crosswalk(tract_crosswalk, tract_relationships)
```

# 5. Review geographic diagnostics

## 5.1 Summarize tracts and relationships

Tract counts and relationship counts have different grains. Report both, with
consistent percentages based on all source 2020 tracts. The zero-land count
below is a count of relationships where either tract's land total is zero.

The count summaries explicitly use `dplyr::count()` because `matrixStats`,
loaded by other pipeline notebooks, provides a different `count()` that can
mask it in a shared R session.

```{r summarize-classification}
tract_summary <- tract_crosswalk |>
  summarise(
    n_2020_tracts = n(), n_consistent = sum(geo_consistent == 1),
    pct_consistent = 100 * mean(geo_consistent == 1),
    n_tracts_with_zero_land_relationship = sum(zero_land_area == 1)
  )
classification_counts <- tract_crosswalk |>
  dplyr::count(relationship_class, name = "n_2020_tracts")
relationship_summary <- tract_relationships |>
  summarise(
    n_relationships = n(), n_2010_tracts = n_distinct(tr2010_id),
    n_zero_land_relationships = sum(zero_land_area == 1),
    n_zero_land_intersections = sum(arealand_part == 0),
    n_non_california_2010_relationships = sum(!startsWith(tr2010_id, "06"))
  )
consistent_geoid_counts <- tract_crosswalk |>
  filter(geo_consistent == 1) |>
  dplyr::count(same_geoid, name = "n_consistent_tracts")
consistent_changed_geoids <- tract_crosswalk |>
  filter(geo_consistent == 1, same_geoid == 0) |>
  select(tr2020_id, tr2010_id, arealand_2020, arealand_2010, arealand_part)
mixed_relationship_tracts <- tract_relationships |>
  group_by(tr2020_id) |>
  summarise(n_pair_classes = n_distinct(relationship_class), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_pair_classes > 1L)
print(tract_summary, width = Inf)
print(classification_counts, n = Inf)
print(relationship_summary, width = Inf)
print(consistent_geoid_counts)
print(consistent_changed_geoids, n = Inf)
report_n(mixed_relationship_tracts, "Mixed pair-class tracts assigned many_to_many")
stopifnot("Class counts do not cover every 2020 tract" =
            sum(classification_counts$n_2020_tracts) == nrow(tract_crosswalk))
```

## 5.2 Summarize target counties and one-to-one exclusions

### Decision: Separate positive-land mismatches from zero-land exclusions

A candidate passes **both** partner-count conditions. Count candidates rejected
by the complete consistency rule, separating pairs with either tract land total
equal to zero from positive-land pairs whose intersection differs from either
tract's total. Zero-land cases receive the zero-land reason even if their area
values also differ; the two reasons are mutually exclusive. GEOID equality does
not enter these diagnostics.

`one_to_one_land_summary` reports statewide counts. `target_region_summary` and
`target_county_summary` show all five classes, percent consistent, candidates,
and rejection reasons for the two regions and all 14 target counties. Absent
classes count as zero; a county with no source tracts has zero counts and an
undefined (`NA`) consistent percentage. The rejected-pair table retains both
GEOIDs and land areas; non-target counties are identified by their state/county
FIPS rather than assigned to a target region. All additions are notebook-only.

```{r summarize-target-counties}
tract_land_diagnostics <- add_tract_land_diagnostics(tract_crosswalk) |>
  mutate(county_fips = substr(tr2020_id, 3, 5))
one_to_one_land_summary <- summarize_tract_classification(tract_land_diagnostics)
target_tract_diagnostics <- tract_land_diagnostics |>
  inner_join(target_county_lookup, by = "county_fips", relationship = "many-to-one")
expected_target_n <- sum(tract_land_diagnostics$county_fips %in% target_county_lookup$county_fips)
report_n(target_tract_diagnostics, "Target-county diagnostic subset (no row multiplication)", expected_target_n)
assert_unique_key(target_tract_diagnostics, "tr2020_id", "Target diagnostic tracts")
stopifnot(nrow(target_tract_diagnostics) == expected_target_n)

target_county_summary <- target_county_lookup |>
  left_join(
    summarize_tract_classification(target_tract_diagnostics, c("region", "county", "county_fips")),
    by = c("region", "county", "county_fips"), relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("n_"), ~ coalesce(.x, 0L))) |>
  arrange(region, county)
target_region_summary <- target_county_lookup |>
  distinct(region) |>
  left_join(summarize_tract_classification(target_tract_diagnostics, "region"),
            by = "region", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("n_"), ~ coalesce(.x, 0L))) |>
  arrange(region)
report_n(target_county_summary, "County summary (one row per configured county)", nrow(target_county_lookup))
report_n(target_region_summary, "Region summary (one row per configured region)", n_distinct(target_county_lookup$region))
county_rollup <- target_county_summary |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("n_"), sum), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(region)
stopifnot("County counts do not reconcile with region counts" = identical(
  county_rollup, select(target_region_summary, region, starts_with("n_"))
))

one_to_one_rejected_pairs <- tract_land_diagnostics |>
  filter(one_to_one_candidate, geo_consistent == 0) |>
  left_join(target_county_lookup, by = "county_fips", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(county = coalesce(county, paste0("FIPS 06", county_fips)),
         region = coalesce(region, "Outside target counties")) |>
  select(tr2020_id, tr2010_id, region, county, county_fips,
         arealand_2020, arealand_2010, arealand_part, rejection_reason)
report_n(one_to_one_rejected_pairs, "Rejected one-to-one pairs (one row per rejected tract)",
         one_to_one_land_summary$n_one_to_one_rejected)
stopifnot(nrow(one_to_one_rejected_pairs) == one_to_one_land_summary$n_one_to_one_rejected,
          "Diagnostic construction altered the statewide crosswalk" = identical(
            select(tract_land_diagnostics, all_of(names(tract_crosswalk))), tract_crosswalk
          ))
print(one_to_one_land_summary, width = Inf)
print(target_region_summary, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(target_county_summary, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(one_to_one_rejected_pairs, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

## 5.3 Inspect overlap shares on changed relationships

Summarize the complete pair table so multi-partner relationships remain visible.
For each share, retain non-consistent relationships with that share's own
positive denominator. Empty groups report `NA` summaries, never infinities.

```{r summarize-overlap}
nonconsistent_share_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(c("2020", "2010"), function(vintage) {
  area <- tract_relationships[[paste0("arealand_", vintage)]]
  keep <- tract_relationships$geo_consistent == 0 & area > 0
  values <- tract_relationships[[paste0("share_", vintage, "_land")]][keep]
  stopifnot("Invalid pair overlap share" = all(is.finite(values) & values >= 0 & values <= 1))
  quantiles <- if (length(values)) {
    unname(quantile(values, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)))
  } else rep(NA_real_, 5L)
  tibble(share = paste0("share_", vintage, "_land"), n_relationships = length(values),
         mean = if (length(values)) mean(values) else NA_real_,
         min = quantiles[1], p25 = quantiles[2], median = quantiles[3],
         p75 = quantiles[4], max = quantiles[5])
}))
print(nonconsistent_share_summary, width = Inf)
```

## 5.4 Report source coverage and land-area reconciliation

### Decision: Report incomplete 2010 coverage without changing relationships

The California file includes 2020 California destinations and some 2010
partners outside California. Reverse counts describe this file's universe.
Report source land sums by vintage; incomplete 2010 coverage is diagnostic and
does not trigger renormalization, filtering, national-file retrieval, or an
alternative consistency rule. Full land coverage of 2020 tracts is expected;
any 2020 mismatch or sum exceeding a tract total stops execution for review.

```{r source-coverage-diagnostics}
non_california_2010_relationships <- tract_relationships |>
  filter(!startsWith(tr2010_id, "06")) |>
  select(tr2020_id, tr2010_id, arealand_2010, arealand_part)
print(non_california_2010_relationships, n = Inf)
land_reconciliation <- bind_rows(lapply(c("2020", "2010"), function(vintage) {
  tract_relationships |>
    group_by(tract_id = .data[[paste0("tr", vintage, "_id")]]) |>
    summarise(tract_land = first(.data[[paste0("arealand_", vintage)]]),
              intersection_land = sum(arealand_part), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(vintage = vintage, difference = intersection_land - tract_land)
}))
land_reconciliation_counts <- land_reconciliation |>
  group_by(vintage) |>
  summarise(n_tracts = n(), n_incomplete = sum(difference < 0),
            n_excess = sum(difference > 0), .groups = "drop")
land_reconciliation_differences <- land_reconciliation |> filter(difference != 0)
print(land_reconciliation_counts)
print(land_reconciliation_differences, n = Inf)
if (any(land_reconciliation$vintage == "2010" & land_reconciliation$difference < 0)) {
  cat("REVIEW: 2010 land totals are not fully represented in this California source;",
      "relationships and exact classification are retained.\n")
}
stopifnot("Intersection sums exceed tract land totals" = all(land_reconciliation$difference <= 0),
          "Incomplete 2020 source land coverage" =
            all(land_reconciliation$difference[land_reconciliation$vintage == "2020"] == 0))
```

# 6. Save and validate the output

## 6.1 Validate and save the new crosswalk

The output retains every source 2020 key, and consistent rows have unique,
nonmissing 2010 keys and exactly unit shares. Recheck these assertions before
writing, and ensure the source has not changed during execution.

```{r save-crosswalk}
assert_tract_crosswalk(tract_crosswalk, tract_relationships)
stopifnot("Raw source changed during execution" =
            identical(unname(tools::md5sum(source_path)), source_md5))
save_tract_crosswalk(tract_crosswalk, output_path, overwrite = overwrite_output)
report_n(tract_crosswalk, "Tract crosswalk saved", n_distinct(source_relationships$tr2020_id))
```

## 6.2 Reload and validate keys, missingness, types, and ranges

Pair-specific missingness is intentional for multi-partner tracts; zero
denominators also produce missing shares. Required tract-level fields cannot be
missing. Verify saved column order, storage types, and every value, then repeat
key, membership, classification, and exact-consistency checks. Numeric summaries
include counts, flags, shares, and land areas; no empirical row count is hardcoded.

```{r validate-saved-crosswalk}
saved_crosswalk <- arrow::read_feather(output_path)
report_n(saved_crosswalk, "Tract crosswalk reloaded", nrow(tract_crosswalk))
assert_same_schema(saved_crosswalk, tract_crosswalk, "Saved tract crosswalk")
stopifnot("Feather round trip changed values or row order" = identical(saved_crosswalk, tract_crosswalk))
assert_tract_crosswalk(saved_crosswalk, tract_relationships)
output_missingness <- saved_crosswalk |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x))))
print(output_missingness, width = Inf)
print_numeric_summary(saved_crosswalk, "Saved tract crosswalk")
```
